parakeet: How does the system survive for 2,000 years when its core promises don't match reality? It relies on a very specific, brilliant theological maneuver. To protect these massive cosmic claims from being debunked, Christianity does one of two things. It either moves the victory into the invisible spiritual realm or it kicks it down the field into the distant future. Notice the pattern. Jesus defeated death, but you still die now. Jesus conquered the grave, but your resurrection happens later. Jesus defeated hell, but people still go there today. Jesus conquered sin, but you still have to struggle with it every morning. Jesus saved the world, but only if you happen to sign the conditional waiver of belief. By doing this, every single metric of success gets postponed, spiritualized, or made entirely conditional. And this isn't a modern patch on the religion. This clever damage control is baked into the foundation. We see the writers of the New Testament scrambling to build this exact escape hatch as early as the first century. In 1 Corinthians 15, Paul is forced to admit that the actual end comes later, only after Jesus eventually abolishes all rule, authority, and power. He has to awkwardly clarify that death is actually the last enemy to be destroyed. The writer of Hebrews captures this exact existential whiplash in a single stunningly honest sentence in chapter 2. You have put all things in subjection under his feet, but now we do not yet see all things subjected to him. Read that again. All things are subjected to him, but we don't see all things subjected to him. That is the grand theological escape hatch. Christianity announces an absolute total victory in the present tense, but pushes 100% of the tangible evidence into a future that never arrives. The claim is always immediate. The proof is always deferred.
